decisions.reason: Uses profile-introspection.txt LinkType Junction, Target E:\dev\dsh-attach-input and the cordis.patch.yml link marker to establish the profile entry resolves to the repo working tree, concludes repo edits already change the installed copy so copying through the junction is unnecessary and self-referential, and explicitly contrasts this with a copied dependency installation.

Relates copy-session.txt EBUSY and the maintainer thread to the running dsh host holding the loaded lib files/module state, notes closing the browser tab cannot release a host-owned lock, and separately explains stale browser-cache delivery requiring host restart plus a cache-bypassing hard refresh, without conflating caching with a filesystem lock.

Explains that renaming via the junction renamed the sole source files so the later Copy-Item found no source; recovery renames client.js.old2/index.js.old2 back to their original names (contents preserved), verifies with node --check on both files, and stops the host first as a precaution.

Gives the semantic order: fully stop the host, restart the dsh web host so new server and served client code load, then hard-refresh/bypass the browser cache, then verify the new hover-preview feature, fresh Network fetch, new host route, and absence of load errors; syntax checks are positioned before activation, not as activation.

Prescribes inspecting the actual profile entry with Get-Item LinkType/Target and the cordis.patch.yml link marker before any file operation, branches the procedure on linked versus copied install, and explains the generic copy-into-node_modules advice assumed an independent copy and thus caused the incident.

caps.reason: The final recovery and deployment plan restores names in place and deploys by editing the repo with no copy step onto the junction target, never deletes the .old2 backups (it renames them back), and never treats the two paths as independent copies.

The plan's affirmative activation procedure requires fully stopping and restarting the dsh host before the browser hard refresh; browser refresh alone is only described as the user's failed earlier attempt, not recommended.
